newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end weak on thin interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end weak on thin interest.

text.p: The Singapore stock market suffered from a lack of trading incentives and ended weaker on Monday despite the firmer trend on Wall Street.
"It's been very quiet with the market trading sideways and no good news expected," said one dealer.
Players also awaited Singapore's April industrial production figures due later in the day for a clearer indication of the economic health, he said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 2.09 points down at 2,030.21. Volume was around 100 million shares with 125 gainers and 197 losers.
Hong Kong-based HongKong Land Holdings Ltd, Jardine Matheson Holdings and Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd hogged the actives.
The three institutions which issued call warrants on the companies on Friday remained active buyers of the stocks.
Put warrants of Jardine Strategic, which give holders right to sell the stock at US$3.80 when they expire next month, lost 75 percent to US$0.005 as the stock ended at US$3.98.
Foreign tranches of SIA Ltd and Jardine Matheson led losers, shedding S$0.30 and US$0.25 to S$12.30 and US$8.05 respectively.
Potential merger candidate, Malaysian timber-related company North Borneo rose S$1.60 to S$20.20.
